title: Radiopathomics deep learning predicts biliary COX-2 expression in pediatric maljunction
summary: In a retrospective study of 219 children with pancreaticobiliary maljunction, a deep learning radiopathomics model combining CT and H&E histology features predicted biliary COX-2 expression (immunohistochemistry reference) with AUCs of 0.851 in an internal test set (n=71) and 0.841 in an external test set (n=44) from a second center. Single-modality radiomics, deep learning radiomics and pathomics models reached AUCs of 0.532-0.602, 0.658-0.660 and 0.787-0.805. The authors state that prospective multicenter studies with larger cohorts are needed.
ai_technology: Deep learning radiopathomics model integrating portal venous-phase CT and H&E histopathology features to predict COX-2 expression

evidence.tested: Retrospective internal test (n=71) and external-center test (n=44) against immunohistochemistry-measured COX-2 expression.
evidence.unknown: Generalizability beyond two centers, prospective performance and any effect on postoperative management; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Combines radiomic, deep learning and pathomic signatures into one classifier predicting a biopsy-defined molecular marker.
